newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Novus says Indonesia oil output up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Novus says Indonesia oil output up.

text.p: Novus Petroleum Ltd said on Monday the Southeast Sumatra production sharing contract (psc) in Indonesia was currently producing crude oil at an average rate of 153,000 barrels a day, up 12 percent from the 1995 average.

The take for Novus, which holds a 3.72 percent stake in the psc is 5,700 barrels a day, it said. The increase is the result in part of infill drilling programmes, particularly recent drilling of horizontal wells capable of producing 7,000 to 10,000 barrels of oil a day each, Novus said.
The block has total expected recoverable reserves of over 1.1 billion barrels, of which about 400 million barrels are yet to be recovered, Novus said.
Maxus Southeast Sumatra Inc holds a 55.6752 percent incterst in the block and is the operator.

The next largest stakeholder is Inpex Sumatra Inc, with 13.067444 percent, followed by Respol Exploration, 9.8657 percent, CIECO, 8.90859 percent, Deminex Sumatra, 5.0 percent and Warrior international, 3.7657 percent.
